heading_en: Roman commanders were never extraordinarily punished for errors
thesis: Rome never punished its generals extraordinarily for errors or ignorance, because commanders must deliberate with a free mind, unburdened by fear of punishment, for warfare is already difficult and dangerous enough.
thesis_quote: lo avere l’animo libero ed espedito, e sanza altri estrinseci rispetti nel pigliare i partiti

propositions.statement: If harsh punishments for defeat were added to the inherent burdens of command, no captain could deliberate vigorously amid so many fears.
propositions.quote: egli era inpossibile che quello capitano intra tanti sospetti potessi deliberare strenuamente

propositions.statement: The Romans chastised errors of malice mildly, and errors of ignorance they did not punish at all but rewarded and honored.
propositions.quote: se il loro errore fusse stato per malizia, e’ lo gastigavano umanamente; se gli era per ignoranza, non che lo punissono, e’ lo premiavano ed onoravano

propositions.statement: The ignominy of defeat is itself sufficient punishment for a commander, so no greater penalty should be added to terrify him.
propositions.quote: giudicando essi che a questi tali fusse assai pena la ignominia dello avere perduto, non li vollono con altra maggiore pena sbigottire

episodes.description: Sergius and Verginius, each commanding part of the army besieging Veii, refused out of rivalry to aid one another and were punished only with fines rather than death.
episodes.quote: Erano Sergio e Virginio a campo a Veio, ciascuno preposto a una parte dello esercito

episodes.description: After Varro's temerity caused the Roman defeat at Cannae, the whole senatorial order went to meet him and thanked him for not despairing of Rome instead of punishing him.
episodes.quote: per la temerità del quale sendo rotti i Romani a Canne da Annibale

episodes.description: When the dictator Papirius Cursor wanted to execute Fabius for fighting the Samnites against his orders, Fabius' father argued that the Roman people had never so treated even defeated commanders.
episodes.quote: Quando Papirio Cursore voleva fare morire Fabio, per avere, contro al suo comandamento, combattuto co’ Sanniti

notes: The Cannae/Varro episode falls outside Livy's first decade (Livy 22.61); candidate given on name-match.

heading_en: A republic or prince should not defer benefits until times of necessity
thesis: Benefits granted to the people only when danger compels them earn no gratitude, so a state must win over its people before adversity arrives rather than relying on the exceptional Roman success with Porsenna.
thesis_quote: non sia alcuno che, confidatosi in questo esemplo, differisca ne’ tempi de’ pericoli a guadagnarsi il popolo

propositions.statement: The people will judge benefits conceded under duress as owed to your adversaries, not to you, and will feel no obligation.
propositions.quote: l’universale giudicherà non avere quel bene da te, ma dagli avversari tuoi

propositions.statement: Whoever holds a state must consider in advance what adverse times may come and which men he will then need, and live with them accordingly.
propositions.quote: debbe qualunque tiene stato, così republica come principe, considerare innanzi, quali tempi gli possono venire addosso contrari, e di quali uomini ne’ tempi avversi si può avere di bisogno

propositions.statement: Whoever waits until danger arrives to regain men with benefits not only fails to secure himself but accelerates his own ruin.
propositions.quote: non solamente non se ne assicura, ma accelera la sua rovina

episodes.description: When Porsenna attacked Rome to restore the Tarquins, the Senate, fearing the plebs might prefer kings to war, relieved them of the salt tax and every burden, and the people endured siege, famine, and war.
episodes.quote: quando Porsenna venne a assaltare Roma per rimettere i Tarquinii

notes: Machiavelli explains the Roman success as exceptional: the state was new and the memory of royal abuses fresh.

heading_en: When an evil has grown within or against a state, it is better to temporize than to strike at it
thesis: Once a danger inside or against a republic has grown great enough to frighten everyone, it is safer to temporize with it than to try to extinguish it, since direct opposition usually increases its force.
thesis_quote: è molto più sicuro partito temporeggiarsi con quello, che tentare di estinguerlo

propositions.statement: Those who try to quench a grown evil almost always make its forces greater and accelerate the harm they feared.
propositions.quote: coloro che tentano di ammorzarlo fanno le sue forze maggiori, e fanno accelerare quel male che da quello si sospettava

propositions.statement: Such evils are hard to recognize at birth because men naturally favor the beginnings of things, especially virtuous-seeming works of young men.
propositions.quote: E tanto è più difficile il conoscere questi inconvenienti quando e’ nascono, quanto e’ pare più naturale agli uomini favorire sempre i principii delle cose

propositions.statement: One should weigh the forces of the malady: attack it without reserve only if sufficient to cure it, otherwise leave it alone entirely.
propositions.quote: Ma si debbano considerare bene le forze del malore, e quando ti vedi sufficiente a sanare quello, metterviti sanza rispetto; altrimenti lasciarlo stare, né in alcun modo tentarlo

episodes.description: Some forty neighboring peoples conspired against the rising Roman republic, which responded by creating the Dictator, an office that overcame the danger and benefited Rome thereafter.
episodes.quote: congiurarono bene quaranta popoli contro a Roma

episodes.description: Florentine citizens, ignoring Niccolò da Uzzano's counsel, moved openly against Cosimo de' Medici and expelled him, whereupon his party recalled him and made him prince of the republic.
episodes.quote: si feciono forti contro a Cosimo, e lo cacciorono da Firenze

episodes.description: Caesar's virtue, first favored by Pompey and others, turned into a source of fear too late, and the remedies attempted against him accelerated the ruin of the Roman republic.
episodes.quote: Pompeio aveva tardi cominciato a temere Cesare

heading_en: Dictatorial authority did good, not harm, to the Roman republic
thesis: The dictatorship, being given by public orders for a limited time and purpose, always benefited Rome; it was authority seized by citizens through prolonged commands, not freely granted magistracies, that enslaved the city.
thesis_quote: e’ non fu il nome né il grado del Dittatore che facesse serva Roma, ma fu l’autorità presa dai cittadini per la lunghezza dello imperio

propositions.statement: Magistracies and authorities created by extraordinary ways harm republics, not those that come by ordinary ways.
propositions.quote: e’ nuocono alle republiche i magistrati che si fanno e l’autoritadi che si dànno per vie istraordinarie, non quelle che vengono per vie ordinarie

propositions.statement: It is forces that easily acquire names, not names that acquire forces.
propositions.quote: e’ sono le forze che facilmente si acquistano i nomi, non i nomi le forze

propositions.statement: The dictator's short term, limited powers, and the uncorrupted Roman people made it impossible for him to exceed his bounds and harm the city.
propositions.quote: raccozzato il breve tempo della sua dittatura, e le autorità limitate che egli aveva, ed il popolo romano non corrotto; era impossibile ch’egli uscisse de’ termini suoi

propositions.statement: Republics that lack recourse to a dictator or similar emergency authority will always be ruined in grave emergencies, since ordinary institutions move too slowly.
propositions.quote: quelle republiche, le quali negli urgenti pericoli non hanno rifugio o al Dittatore o a simili autoritadi, sempre ne’ gravi accidenti rovineranno

episodes.description: Caesar, the first tyrant of Rome, commanded the city under the dictatorial title, which led some writers to blame the institution itself for Rome's tyranny.
episodes.quote: il primo tiranno che fosse in quella città la comandò sotto questo titolo dittatorio

episodes.description: The Venetian republic reserves authority to a few citizens who, in urgent needs, may decide in common accord without wider consultation.
episodes.quote: la Republica viniziana, la quale intra le moderne republiche è eccellente, ha riservato autorità a pochi cittadini

episodes.description: In later times the Romans, instead of naming a dictator, gave emergency authority to the consul with the formula 'Videat Consul, ne Respublica quid detrimenti capiat'.
episodes.quote: i Romani usassono, in cambio del Dittatore, di dare tale autorità al Console

notes: Includes the Latin formula of the senatus consultum ultimum, which postdates Livy's first decade narrative context.

heading_en: Why the creation of the Decemvirate harmed Roman liberty although freely elected
thesis: Even authority given by free public suffrage becomes dangerous when it is absolute, long in duration, and unguarded by other institutions, as the Decemvirate proved in contrast with the dictatorship.
thesis_quote: quando e’ si dia autorità libera, col tempo lungo, chiamando il tempo lungo uno anno o più, sempre fia pericolosa

propositions.statement: The dictator was kept good because the Senate, consuls, and tribunes retained their authority and stood as his guard, preventing him from leaving the straight path.
propositions.quote: il Senato, i Consoli, i Tribuni, restando con l’autorità loro, venivano a essere come sua guardia, a farlo non uscire della via diritta

propositions.statement: The Ten, left alone without consuls, tribunes, or appeal to the people, had no one to observe them and so could become insolent.
propositions.quote: trovandosi soli, sanza Consoli, sanza Tribuni, sanza appellagione al Popolo; e per questo non venendo ad avere chi gli osservasse

propositions.statement: An uncorrupted citizenry is no safeguard, because absolute authority corrupts the matter in a very short time and makes itself friends and partisans.
propositions.quote: una autorità assoluta in brevissimo tempo corrompe la materia e si fa amici e partigiani

episodes.description: The ten citizens elected by the Roman people to make laws became tyrants over time and seized the city's liberty without restraint, moved by the ambition of Appius in their second year.
episodes.quote: la elezione dei dieci cittadini creati dal Popolo romano per fare le leggi in Roma

notes: Sparta's kings and Venice's doges are cited as long-term authorities kept good by institutional guards; treated as institutional comparisons, not episodes.

heading_en: Citizens who have held higher honors should not disdain lesser ones
thesis: Roman greatness rested partly on citizens willingly obeying men they had once commanded and serving in armies they had led, a custom contrary to modern opinion, as in Venice, and vital to free government.
thesis_quote: non stimavano così disonorevole ubbidire ora a chi altra volta essi avevano comandato, e trovarsi a servire in quello esercito del quale erano stati principi

propositions.statement: A republic should place more hope in a citizen who descends from a great office to govern a lesser one than in one who rises from a lesser to a greater.
propositions.quote: più speranza debbe avere una republica, e più confidare in uno cittadino che da uno grado grande scenda a governare uno minore che in quello che da uno minore salga a governare uno maggiore

propositions.statement: Had Rome followed the Venetian custom that an ex-consul never serve except as consul, infinite harms to free life would have resulted from inexperienced and unchecked new men.
propositions.quote: che chi era stato una volta Consolo non volesse mai più andare negli eserciti se non Consolo, ne sarebbero nate infinite cose in disfavore del vivere libero

episodes.description: The consuls Marcus Fabius and Gnaeus Manilius won a most glorious battle against the Veientes and Etruscans, in which Quintus Fabius, consul the previous year, was killed serving under his brother.
episodes.quote: Avevano i Romani fatto Marco Fabio e G. Manilio consoli, e vinta una gloriosissima giornata contro a’ Veienti

heading_en: The scandals born in Rome from the agrarian law
thesis: The agrarian law, born of plebeian ambition once necessity was satisfied, convulsed Rome whenever raised and ultimately destroyed the republic, showing that retrospective laws against ancient customs are most scandalous.
thesis_quote: Da questo nacque il morbo che partorì la contenzione della legge agraria, che infine fu causa della distruzione della Republica

propositions.statement: Whenever men no longer fight from necessity, they fight from ambition, which never abandons them at any rank they reach.
propositions.quote: qualunque volta è tolto agli uomini il combattere per necessità, combattono per ambizione

propositions.statement: Because desire always exceeds the power of acquiring, men remain discontented with what they possess, which drives enmity and war and the variation of fortunes.
propositions.quote: essendo sempre maggiore il desiderio che la potenza dello acquistare, ne risulta la mala contentezza di quello che si possiede

propositions.statement: Well-ordered republics must keep the public treasury rich and their citizens poor.
propositions.quote: le republiche bene ordinate hanno a tenere ricco il publico e gli loro cittadini, poveri

propositions.statement: Making a law that reaches far back to remove a disorder already grown in a republic is ill-considered and only accelerates the evil, whereas temporizing delays or extinguishes it.
propositions.quote: a volere levar via uno disordine cresciuto in una republica, e per questo fare una legge che riguardi assai indietro, è partito male considerato

episodes.description: To defuse a dispute over the agrarian law, a colony was sent from Rome to the territory of Antium, and Livy notes that hardly anyone could be found to give his name to go.
episodes.quote: con difficultà si trovò in Roma chi desse il nome per ire in detta colonia

episodes.description: The agrarian law lay dormant until the Gracchi reawakened it, finding its opponents' power doubled, kindling such hatred between plebs and Senate that it came to arms and blood.
episodes.quote: questa legge stette come addormentata infino ai Gracchi; da’ quali essendo poi svegliata, rovinò al tutto la libertà romana

episodes.description: The plebs made Marius consul four times and the nobility, lacking other remedy, raised up Sulla as head of its party, leading to civil wars won by the nobility.
episodes.quote: e volse la sua riputazione a Mario tanto che la lo fece quattro volte consule

episodes.description: The same humors revived with Caesar heading Marius' party and Pompey Sulla's; Caesar prevailed and became Rome's first tyrant, so the city was never free again.
episodes.quote: fattosi Cesare capo della parte di Mario, e Pompeio di quella di Silla, venendo alle mani, rimase superiore Cesare

notes: Machiavelli explicitly names Tito Livio for the Antium colony remark; the specific chapter (Livy 3.1) is inferred, as he cites no book or chapter number.

heading_en: Weak republics are irresolute and decide only from necessity
thesis: Weak republics cannot resolve on doubtful courses and take good decisions only when forced, unlike the Roman Senate, which knew how to make a virtue of necessity and keep authority over its own deliberations.
thesis_quote: le republiche inresolute non pigliono mai partiti buoni, se non per forza, perché la debolezza loro non le lascia mai deliberare dove è alcuno dubbio

propositions.statement: By licensing what its allies would do anyway, the Senate ensured that having disobeyed from necessity they would not grow accustomed to disobeying from choice.
propositions.quote: acciocché, avendo disubbidito per necessità, non si avvezzassero a disubbidire per elezione

propositions.statement: A prudent government always judges things as they should be judged and takes the least bad course as the best.
propositions.quote: sempre giudicò le cose come si debbano giudicare, e sempre prese il meno reo partito per migliore

propositions.statement: Had Beaumont acted like Imbalt and accepted the surrender on his own terms, Florence would have had Pisa as it had Arezzo.
propositions.quote: se Beumonte fosse stato simile a Imbalt, si sarebbe avuto Pisa come Arezzo

episodes.description: During a grave pestilence in Rome, the Volsci and Aequi attacked the Latins and Hernici, and the Senate, unable to defend them, authorized them to arm and defend themselves.
episodes.quote: risposero che pigliassero partito di difendersi da loro medesimi e con le loro armi

episodes.description: Duke Valentino, after taking Faenza and bending Bologna to his terms, sent to Florence to demand passage for himself and his army, and the irresolute Florentines handled it dishonorably.
episodes.quote: mandò in Firenze uno suo uomo a domandare il passo per sé e per lo esercito suo

episodes.description: In 1500 Pisan envoys offered Beaumont the city for the French army under promise of a four-month delay before handover to Florence; the Florentines refused out of distrust and the siege ended in shame.
episodes.quote: vennono oratori Pisani a Beumonte, e gli offerirono di dare la città allo esercito francese

episodes.description: In 1502, after Florence refused a similar accord with rebellious Arezzo, monsignor Imbalt concluded it himself without the Florentine commissioners and entered Arezzo with his troops.
episodes.quote: cominciò a tenere le pratiche dello accordo da sé, sanza partecipazione de’ Commessari

notes: Livy candidate for the pestilence episode (3.6) based on the pestilence and the Hernici/Latini appeal; medium certainty on exact chapter.

heading_en: The same accidents are often seen among different peoples
thesis: Since all cities and peoples have the same desires and humors in every age, whoever diligently examines past events can foresee the future in any republic and apply the remedies the ancients used.
thesis_quote: in tutte le città ed in tutti i popoli sono quegli medesimi desiderii e quelli medesimi omori, e come vi furono sempre

propositions.statement: Whoever diligently examines past things can foresee future ones in every republic and apply the remedies used by the ancients or devise new ones from the similarity of events.
propositions.quote: gli è facil cosa, a chi esamina con diligenza le cose passate, prevedere in ogni republica le future, e farvi quegli rimedi che dagli antichi sono stati usati

propositions.statement: Because these considerations are neglected by readers and unknown to rulers, the same scandals recur in every age.
propositions.quote: queste considerazioni sono neglette, o non intese da chi legge, o, se le sono intese, non sono conosciute da chi governa

episodes.description: After 1494 Florence, blaming the Dieci della guerra for its costly war to recover Pisa, let the magistracy lapse, lost Arezzo and other places, and then recognized the fever, not the physician, was the cause and restored the Ten.
episodes.quote: ravvedutosi il popolo dello errore suo, e come la cagione del male era la febbre e non il medico, rifece il magistrato de’ Dieci

episodes.description: The tribune Terentillus first proposed a law to create five men to examine and limit the consuls' power, greatly alarming the nobility.
episodes.quote: Il primo che tentò questa legge, fu uno Terentillo tribuno

episodes.description: The tribunes' obstinacy extinguished the consular name and Rome created tribunes with consular power instead, hating the name more than the authority, until the error was recognized and consuls were restored.
episodes.quote: più tosto creare Tribuni con potestà consolare, che Consoli: tanto avevano più in odio il nome che l’autorità loro

heading_en: The creation of the Decemvirate in Rome and what is notable in it
thesis: The Decemvirate shows how republics are lost: when people and nobles, instead of agreeing on a law for liberty, each favor one man to crush the other side, tyranny immediately arises.
thesis_quote: E quando e’ non convengano a fare una legge in favore della libertà, ma gettasi qualcuna delle parti a favorire uno, allora è che subito la tirannide surge

propositions.statement: Most tyrannies in cities are born from the people's excessive desire to be free and the nobles' excessive desire to command.
propositions.quote: questo è da troppo desiderio del popolo, d’essere libero, e da troppo desiderio de’ nobili, di comandare

propositions.statement: When a people gives reputation to a shrewd man so that he may beat those it hates, he will always become tyrant of that city.
propositions.quote: quando uno popolo si conduce a fare questo errore, di dare riputazione a uno, perché batta quelli che egli ha in odio, e che quello uno sia savio, sempre interverrà ch’e’ diventerà tiranno di quella città

propositions.statement: Tyrants who have the populace as friend and the great as enemies are more secure, their violence being sustained by greater forces.
propositions.quote: quegli tiranni che hanno amico l’universale ed inimici i grandi, sono più sicuri, per essere la loro violenza sostenuta da maggiori forze

propositions.statement: To hold anything by violence, the one who forces must be more powerful than the one who is forced.
propositions.quote: a volere con violenza tenere una cosa, bisogna che sia più potente chi sforza che chi è sforzato

episodes.description: Rome sent Spurius Postumius with two other citizens to Athens for copies of the laws Solon gave that city, as a foundation for the Roman laws.
episodes.quote: mandarono, d’accordo, Spurio Pestumio, con duoi altri Cittadini, a Atene

episodes.description: Ten citizens, among them the shrewd and restless Appius Claudius, were created for a year to make the laws, with all other magistracies removed and appeal to the people abolished.
episodes.quote: crearono dieci cittadini per uno anno, intra i quali fu creato Appio Claudio, uomo sagace ed inquieto

episodes.description: Entrusted with proposing the next Ten, Appius seized the impediment as an opportunity and named himself among the first, to the amazement and displeasure of the nobles.
episodes.quote: nominò sé intra i primi, con maraviglia e dispiacere di tutti i nobili

episodes.description: The second Decemvirate showed its pride, beating plebs and Senate alike, and to terrify them increased the lictors from twelve to one hundred twenty.
episodes.quote: in cambio di dodici littori, ne feciono cento venti

episodes.description: War moved by the Sabines and Volsci forced the Ten to convene the Senate, where Valerius and Horatius spoke against their pride.
episodes.quote: i Sabini ed i Volsci mossero guerra a’ Romani

episodes.description: Appius fell in love with Virginia and tried to take her by force; her father Virginius killed her to free her, provoking tumults in Rome and the armies, secession to the Monte Sacro, and the fall of the Ten.
episodes.quote: si innamorò di Virginia, e che, volendola tôrre per forza, il padre Virginio, per liberarla, l’ammazzò

episodes.description: Nabis, tyrant of Sparta, having secured himself against a few nobles and holding the people as friend, defended himself when all Greece and the Roman people assaulted him.
episodes.quote: come bastarono a Nabide, tiranno di Sparta, quando tutta Grecia e il Popolo romano lo assaltò

notes: Contains several unattributed verbatim Latin quotations from Livy (e.g. 'haud gratuitam in tanta superbia comitatem fore', Livy 3.35; 'et inde libertatis captare auram', Livy 3.37) without naming him. Also cites a saying of King Ferrando comparing men to lesser birds of prey.

heading_en: To leap from humility to pride, from mercy to cruelty, without due degrees is imprudent and useless
thesis: Appius' sudden change from friend of the plebs to its proud enemy, made without due intermediate steps, stripped him of old supporters before gaining new ones and ruined his tyranny.
thesis_quote: chi è paruto buono un tempo, e vuole a suo proposito diventar cattivo, lo debbe fare per i debiti mezzi

propositions.statement: One who changes nature must manage occasions so that new favors are gained before the changed nature strips away the old ones, lest authority diminish.
propositions.quote: innanzi che la diversa natura ti tolga de’ favori vecchi, la te ne abbia dati tanti de’ nuovi, che tu non venga a diminuire la tua autorità

propositions.statement: Changing so fast that everyone must recognize the falsity of your mind leaves you discovered and friendless, and you are ruined.
propositions.quote: e farlo tanto presto, che, sanza scusa niuna, ogni uomo avesse a conoscere la fallacia dello animo suo

episodes.description: Appius, having skillfully simulated popularity to win the plebs and secure his reappointment, suddenly changed nature, showing himself the plebs' enemy, proud instead of humane, so that everyone saw his deceit.
episodes.quote: mutare, in uno subito, natura; e, di amico, mostrarsi inimico alla plebe; di umano, superbo

heading_en: How easily men may be corrupted
thesis: The Decemvirate shows how easily even good and well-educated men are corrupted and made of contrary nature by a little ambition or utility, which lawgivers must anticipate.
thesis_quote: quanto facilmente gli uomini si corrompono, e fannosi diventare di contraria natura, quantunque buoni e bene ammaestrati

propositions.statement: However good and well-trained, men are easily corrupted and made to assume a contrary nature.
propositions.quote: quanto facilmente gli uomini si corrompono, e fannosi diventare di contraria natura, quantunque buoni e bene ammaestrati

propositions.statement: Lawgivers of republics and kingdoms should therefore be readier to bridle human appetites and remove all hope of erring with impunity.
propositions.quote: farà tanto più pronti i latori di leggi delle republiche o de’ regni a frenare gli appetiti umani, e tôrre loro ogni speranza di potere impune errare

episodes.description: The young nobles Appius gathered around himself became friends of the tyranny for a little profit that came to them from it.
episodes.quote: quella gioventù che Appio si aveva eletta intorno, cominciò a essere amica della tirannide per uno poco di utilità

episodes.description: Quintus Fabius, one of the second Ten and an excellent man, blinded by a little ambition and persuaded by Appius' malignity, changed his good habits into the worst and became like him.
episodes.quote: Quinto Fabio, uno del numero de’ secondi Dieci, sendo uomo ottimo, accecato da uno poco d’ambizione

heading_en: Those who fight for their own glory are good and faithful soldiers
thesis: Armies content and fighting for their own glory conquer, while those fighting for another's ambition fail, which explains the uselessness of mercenary soldiers and the need to arm one's own subjects.
thesis_quote: quanta differenzia è da uno esercito contento e che combatte per la gloria sua, a quello che è male disposto e che combatte per l’ambizione d’altrui

propositions.statement: Mercenary soldiers, held only by a little stipend, can never be faithful enough or friendly enough to die for their employer.
propositions.quote: i quali non hanno altra cagione che gli tenga fermi, che un poco di stipendio che tu dai loro

propositions.statement: To hold a state, whether republic or kingdom, it is necessary to arm oneself with one's own subjects.
propositions.quote: è necessario, a volere tenere uno stato, a volere mantenere una republica o uno regno, armarsi de’ sudditi suoi

episodes.description: The Roman armies, always victorious under the consuls, always lost under the Decemvirs, and regained their old spirit and success as soon as the Ten were removed and they fought as free men.
episodes.quote: dove gli eserciti romani solevano sempre essere vittoriosi sotto i Consoli, sotto i Decemviri sempre perderono

heading_en: A multitude without a head is useless, and one should not threaten before having the power
thesis: The plebs on the Monte Sacro shows that a multitude without a head is useless, and that it is folly to announce the harm you intend before obtaining the authority or means to do it.
thesis_quote: La qual cosa dimostra appunto la inutilità d’una moltitudine sanza capo

propositions.statement: It is foolishness and imprudence to demand a thing while first declaring the evil one intends to do with it.
propositions.quote: quanta stultizia e poca prudenza è domandare una cosa, e dire prima: io voglio fare il tale male con essa

propositions.statement: One should not show one's mind but seek to obtain one's desire by any means, for having the arms in hand one can then satisfy the appetite.
propositions.quote: non si debbe mostrare l’animo suo, ma vuolsi cercare di ottenere quel suo desiderio in ogni modo

episodes.description: The armed plebs on the Monte Sacro, having no heads, dared not answer the Senate's ambassadors until Virginius had twenty military tribunes created as their chiefs to negotiate.
episodes.quote: per suo ordine si creò venti Tribuni militari, che fossero loro capi, a rispondere e convenire col Senato

episodes.description: The plebs demanded of Valerius and Horatius the restoration of tribunes and appeal, but also that the Ten be handed over to be burned alive, which the envoys condemned as impious.
episodes.quote: che si dessono loro tutti i Dieci che gli volevono ardere vivi

notes: Machiavelli explicitly cites Tito Livio ('E Tito Livio dice') for the observation that the plebs lacked not matter but a spokesman; includes the Latin 'Crudelitatem damnatis, in crudelitatem ruitis'.

heading_en: It is a bad example not to observe a law, above all by its author; and daily renewed injuries are most harmful to a ruler
thesis: Nothing sets a worse example in a republic than making a law and not observing it, especially by its author; and keeping subjects fearful with continually renewed injuries is most damaging to whoever governs.
thesis_quote: io non credo che sia cosa di più cattivo esemplo in una republica, che fare una legge e non la osservare; e tanto più, quanto la non è osservata da chi l’ha fatta

propositions.statement: It is most harmful for a republic or prince to keep subjects' minds suspended and fearful with continual penalties and offenses.
propositions.quote: quanto sia dannoso a una republica o a un principe, tenere con le continove pene ed offese sospesi e paurosi gli animi de’ sudditi

propositions.statement: Men who begin to fear coming to harm secure themselves in dangers in any way they can, becoming bolder and less restrained in attempting new things.
propositions.quote: gli uomini che cominciono a dubitare di avere a capitare male, in ogni modo si assicurano ne’ pericoli, e diventono più audaci, e meno respettivi a tentare cose nuove

propositions.statement: One must either never injure anyone or do the injuries all at one stroke, and then reassure men and give them cause to quiet and settle their minds.
propositions.quote: è necessario o non offendere mai alcuno, o fare le offese a un tratto: e dipoi rassicurare gli uomini

episodes.description: Virginius cited Appius before the people; denied the appeal he himself had destroyed, Appius was imprisoned and killed himself before the day of judgment, though violating the new law of appeal was itself uncivil.
episodes.quote: egli fu incarcerato, ed avanti al dì del giudizio ammazzò se stesso

episodes.description: In post-1494 Florence, Savonarola's hard-won law of appeal to the people was broken when the Signoria condemned five citizens to death for state reasons and denied their appeal, costing the friar his reputation.
episodes.quote: furono condannati a morte dalla Signoria, per conto di stato, cinque cittadini; e volendo quegli appellare, non furono lasciati

episodes.description: After the Decemvirate, continual accusations terrified the whole nobility until the tribune Marcus Duellius decreed that for one year no Roman citizen could be cited or accused, reassuring them.
episodes.quote: fece uno editto, che per uno anno non fusse lecito a alcuno citare o accusare alcuno cittadino romano
